summary: This proposed standard defines an SMTP extension where the client declares the estimated size of a message so the server can decline it, perhaps temporarily, before it is sent. It was replaced by RFC 1653.

eli5.summary: Before sending a big package, you tell the receiver how big it is so they can say no if there is no room. This extension lets email servers do that.

questions: what is the smtp size extension
how does smtp announce message size

subtitle: Lets clients declare message size so servers can reject too-large messages before they arrive.

tldr.problem: Without size information, SMTP servers cannot reject oversized messages until after the entire message has been transmitted, wasting bandwidth and server resources.
tldr.mechanism: This extension adds a SIZE parameter to the MAIL FROM command where clients declare the message size, and servers can advertise their maximum acceptable message size in the EHLO response. This lets servers reject messages early.
tldr.outcome: Clients can now check message size before transmitting and servers can detect over-limit messages before consuming resources. This was replaced by RFC 1653, which consolidated multiple SMTP extensions.

today: RFC 1427 is a Proposed Standard that was replaced by RFC 1653, which consolidated this and related SMTP extensions. The SIZE capability is now part of modern SMTP implementations for efficient message size handling.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
MIME extensions enable the Internet to transmit many kinds of data that were previously unsupported in email, including binary content and various media types. This capability led to much larger message sizes than traditional SMTP had encountered.

The Message Size Declaration extension addresses a practical problem: a server may have limits on how large a message it will accept, and may also lack sufficient temporary storage to buffer an incoming message. Without advance notice of message size, a client could spend substantial time transmitting a message only to have the server reject it due to size or resource constraints. This extension lets servers advertise their limits and clients declare their message size in advance.
sections.eli5: Email servers have limited storage space. If a client tried to send a huge message, the server would have to wait for the whole thing before saying no. This extension lets the server reject it first.

sections.title: Size Declaration Mechanism
sections.content:
The extension uses the EHLO keyword SIZE with an optional numeric parameter indicating the server's fixed maximum message size in bytes. A parameter value of 0 means no fixed limit; an absent parameter means the server is not advertising a limit.

A client can include a SIZE parameter on the extended MAIL FROM command, specifying the estimated size in octets of the message to be transmitted, including headers and body lines with CR-LF pairs but excluding the SMTP data terminator.

Upon receiving the extended MAIL command with a SIZE declaration, the server can reject the message immediately with a permanent error (code 552) if the size exceeds its fixed maximum, or a temporary error (code 452) if the server currently lacks sufficient storage resources but might accept the message later.
sections.eli5: The server says how big a message it can handle. When the client wants to send mail, it tells the server the message size. The server can say okay or no before any data is sent.

sections.title: Client and Server Behavior
sections.content:
The message size is defined as the number of octets including CR-LF pairs but excluding the SMTP DATA command's terminating dot or doubled quoting dots. Clients MUST NOT use the SIZE parameter to determine the end of content in the DATA command; the standard CRLF.CRLF sequence still marks the end.

Servers MUST NOT return a 552 reply code after the DATA transfer phase unless the actual message size exceeds the declared size. However, servers may choose to accept messages somewhat larger than declared. Clients may declare a message smaller than its actual size, but in that case the server is not obligated to accept it even after responding positively to the MAIL command.

The extension supports per-recipient limitations: a server may return a 452 or 552 code in response to a RCPT command based on size constraints for a particular recipient.
sections.eli5: The client estimates the message size. The server can check before reading any data, or check when the recipient is named. Servers can also reject messages that are bigger than declared after they are sent.

sections.title: Security and Denial of Service
sections.content: The size declaration extension can be used to facilitate service denial attacks by making it quicker to devise attacks that exhaust server resources. However, unless implementations are very weak, the extension does not create any new vulnerability beyond what already exists with SMTP. The information itself (declared size) and the extended MAIL command do not fundamentally change the attack surface; they only make specific attacks slightly more convenient.
sections.eli5: Someone could abuse size declarations to attack email servers, but not in a way they couldn't already do with basic SMTP. The extension does not create fundamentally new security risks.
